blocks.why: Normal night at home before the roster opens — bank a full one, the ORD day finishes at 04:00 body time.
Siesta before an afternoon report; I won't see a bed again for about twenty-one hours.
Straight to bed at the hotel — it's 04:45 body time, so sleep comes easily even though the Chicago clock says 22:00.
Second layover night kept on Madrid time; no point dragging the body clock west for one day.
Long afternoon sleep before the all-night eastbound — this is the sleep that actually flies the sector.
Post-redeye nap at home, capped before 18:00 local so I can still sleep tonight.
Full night at home to reset before the BOS pairing.
Short top-up before report — landing in Boston is 23:35 body time.
Sleep on Madrid time at the hotel (19:00 to 03:00 local) — it lines up with my own night and sets up tomorrow's late report.
Big afternoon sleep before a 21:40 local report and an overnight back to base.
Take the edge off after the redeye, then stay up for daylight so the first free night is a proper one.
First recovery night at home after two Atlantic crossings.
Deliberately shorter and earlier — I'm walking the bedtime back for Tuesday's 06:10 report.
Afternoon nap as sleep credit, because nobody really sleeps eight hours before an early.
Early to bed at 21:00 local for a 03:15 departure from the door; expect it to be broken sleep.
Pay back the early start once I'm home, before the LAX night flight tomorrow.
Full night at home — the last normal one before the deepest west trip of the month.
Long pre-duty sleep for an eleven-hour night sector landing at 09:00 body time.
Sleep on arrival at the hotel; it's mid-morning body time so I take what I can get and cut it at six and a half hours.
Afternoon nap in LA to stop the evening falling apart before the main layover night.
Proper LA night, up at 06:30 local — this is the sleep that has to carry me across the whole Madrid night tomorrow.
Quick top-up before report; duty ends after eighteen hours awake and lands in a Madrid morning.
Longer than a nap on purpose — nine time zones back needs a real sleep, then daylight to lock onto Madrid.
Night at home with the clocks going back at 03:00 — an extra hour in bed for free.
Nap before the GRU report; landing is 03:25 body time.
Straight to bed in São Paulo — only four hours off Madrid, so this is close to a normal night.
Nap before the 17:00 local report; the sector runs right through the small hours body time.
Home off the redeye — sleep now, get outside this afternoon, sleep properly tonight.
Full night before the Bogotá pairing, which ends with the worst finish of the month.
Siesta before an afternoon report landing at 04:45 body time.
Bed as soon as I'm in the hotel; 23:45 local Bogotá is 05:45 to me and I'm past my limit.
Short siesta so I can go to bed early tonight without lying awake.
Early night in Bogotá (20:00 to 03:30 local) because tomorrow's duty finishes at 03:00 Madrid time.
Split the sleep and take a second bite before report — I need everything I can carry into that 02:30 landing.
Straight to bed at home after a 03:55 arrival at the door; sleep in and write the morning off.
First proper recovery night of three days off.
Second recovery night — body clock should be back on Madrid by now.
To bed by 22:30 local for a 06:50 departure from the door on Tuesday's BOS.
Early afternoon nap on arrival in Boston after an early start, then out for daylight.
Layover night split between the two clocks — 21:00 to 04:30 local keeps me useful for a late report later.
Same pattern again so tonight's short sleep isn't a shock; up at 04:00 local for a long day.
Three solid hours in the afternoon before a 21:40 local report — the last redeye of the month.
Home off the overnight, and I need to be up early tomorrow, so nap now and keep it short.
Bed at 21:00 local for an 06:00 standby start — awkward with a west-shifted body clock, so lights out early and no screens.
If the standby runs to release, nap after it to clear the early start.
Full night at home; tomorrow's standby is a civilised 13:00 start.
Last night of the period — back onto a normal Madrid pattern.

conflicts.statement: No FTL or fatigue rule set was provided with this roster, so the rule IDs below are my own descriptive labels, not references to your operator's manual. Nothing here is a legality finding — the operator owns that.
options: Send me the operator's FTL/FRM rule set and I'll re-map these against the real rule numbers
Raise any of the items below with the fatigue safety action group in their own language

conflicts.statement: The roster prints a report time for every duty, so I used those directly. They imply 90 minutes before departure on long-haul but only 60 minutes on the 20 Oct MAD-LIS-MAD short-haul day. I have not overridden the printed times, but the inconsistency is worth confirming.
options: Confirm the short-haul reporting offset with crewing before the 20 Oct early
Assume 90 minutes and leave home 30 minutes earlier, which pulls the wake-up back to 02:00Z

conflicts.statement: Report is 06:10 local, meaning the alarm at 04:30 local (02:30Z) and leaving the door at 05:15. Sleep initiated at 21:00 local rarely delivers a full night, so the realistic opportunity here is about six broken hours, not eight.
options: Take the 19 Oct afternoon nap as planned and treat it as part of the sleep budget
Keep 19 Oct completely free of evening commitments and dark by 20:30 local
Flag it as a single early after three days off — the pattern is survivable but the sleep is not

conflicts.statement: TL286 BOG-MAD reports 13:45Z and lands 01:30Z with on-blocks plus 30 finishing 02:00Z (03:00 local). The final three hours are flown squarely inside the 02:00-06:00 body-clock window at the end of a 12h15 duty, and the approach into MAD is the lowest-alertness point of the whole roster.
options: Protect the split sleep on 30 Oct (00:30-08:00Z plus 10:00-11:15Z) rather than running a single block
Plan in-seat controlled rest during the cruise with the other operating crew
Arrange transport home rather than driving after a 03:00 local arrival
If sleep at BOG does not come, call fatigued before report rather than after landing

conflicts.statement: TL435 LAX-MAD reports 18:10Z and finishes 07:25Z — a 13h15 duty that crosses the entire Madrid night after a layover of under 36 hours at nine hours' displacement. The body clock will still be on LAX time, so the descent into MAD happens at roughly 22:00 body time on top of a full waking day.
options: Guard the 05:30-13:30Z LAX night sleep — no early tours, no late dinner
Take the 16:00-17:00Z top-up nap even if you do not feel tired
Split rest in the bunk with the heaviest slice in the second half of the cruise

conflicts.statement: 25-30 Oct runs GRU out-and-back then BOG out-and-back with only 27 Oct between them, giving three overnight finishes into MAD (27 Oct 08:20Z, 31 Oct 02:00Z) plus the 24 Oct LAX finish inside eight days. Cumulative sleep debt builds across this stretch faster than the single days off can clear it.
options: Treat 27 Oct as a sleep day, not an errands day
Ask crewing whether the 28 Oct BOG could start later if the GRU pairing runs late
Log cumulative fatigue if the 31 Oct arrival lands on top of an already short 27 Oct

conflicts.statement: You land at MAD 11:40Z on 6 Nov off an all-night BOS sector, then standby opens at 06:00 local on 7 Nov (05:00Z). That is roughly 17 hours from duty end to standby start, with a body clock still five hours west, so the 21:00 local bedtime on 6 Nov will be fought hard.
options: Keep the 6 Nov recovery nap short and finish it by 16:00Z so the early bedtime is achievable
Ask crewing whether the two reserve days could be swapped so the 13:00 start comes first
If called out early on 7 Nov, declare the preceding sleep opportunity when you accept the assignment

conflicts.statement: Europe ends DST at 03:00 local on 25 Oct (MAD/LIS +2 to +1) and the US ends it on 1 Nov (BOS -4 to -5). Local-time roster entries either side of those dates convert differently, and the 3 Nov MAD-BOS and 5 Nov BOS-MAD are the sectors affected on the US side. All conversions above account for this.
options: Sanity-check the 25 Oct and 3-5 Nov report times against the company crew portal, which normally publishes UTC
Set phone alarms to the station's local time, not a fixed offset, across both transitions
